penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A SpamAssassin plugin or milter requires per-customer installation, server-level configuration, and debugging on self-hosted infrastructure — no automated delivery path exists.

rationale: Self-hosted mail server operators are highly technical and notoriously resistant to paying for tooling they believe they can build themselves; willingness to pay for a SpamAssassin plugin is very low. The buyer (SMB sysadmin or hosting provider) is identifiable but dispersed and hard to reach at scale through allowed channels. Delivery requires per-customer server access and configuration, making autonomous operation impossible. After the fulfillment penalty, the total falls to 2.4, well below threshold.
solution_plan: Not recommended. Delivering a working SpamAssassin plugin to self-hosted mail operators requires hands-on server access, compatibility testing across dozens of stack variants (Postfix versions, OS distributions, SpamAssassin configs), and ongoing maintenance as phishing techniques evolve. This cannot be productized as a hands-off micro-service by a solo non-technical operator. Pass.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy (4 < 7 floor) and buildability_with_ai (4 < 6 floor). Total also below validate threshold. Drop.
